parts.label: (a)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text:
$4k+k+4k+9k=18k=1\implies k=\frac1{18}$ [B1] Shown or implied by probabilities summing to one.
$X=-2,1,2,3$ with respective probabilities $4/18,1/18,4/18,9/18$. [M1] Allow any order or orientation and omitted row headings; require all four $x$-values and at least one probability correct using their $k$; additional values are allowed only with probability zero.
$P(X=-2)=4/18$, $P(X=1)=1/18$, $P(X=2)=4/18$, and $P(X=3)=9/18$. [A1] Require all remaining probabilities correct.
Total: 3

parts.label: (b)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text:
$E(X)=\frac{4(-2)+1(1)+4(2)+9(3)}{18}$ [M1] May be implied in the variance work; accept an unsimplified expression and follow through a distribution totalling $1$ or $0.999$; special case B1 for $28k$.
$\operatorname{Var}(X)=\frac{4(-2)^2+1(1)^2+4(2)^2+9(3)^2}{18}-[E(X)]^2$ [M1] Follow through their table even if it does not total one; with the correct table accept $114/18-[E(X)]^2$; special case B1 for $114k-[E(X)]^2$.
$E(X)=\frac{14}{9},\quad \operatorname{Var}(X)=\frac{317}{81}\approx3.91$ [A1] Both $E(X)$ and $\operatorname{Var}(X)$ must be identified; accept variance from $3.91$ to $3.914$ inclusive.
Total: 3
